note: Pre-registered before implementation, per the standing request. Ranked by expected DTI
improvement per unit of implementation cost. 'status' records what was actually done
this session, not what was hoped for.

validated_this_session.what: Removing dist_visible_fault / visible_fault_dens_5k / visible_fault_dens_20k from the
model. They are computed from the visible catalogue and are exactly zero (or maximal)
on the catalogue pixels that form the training presence set, so a model that sees them
separates the training data and then generalises at chance.

hypotheses.title: Depth-to-conductive-basement and conductivity-surface step lineaments (blind basin-floor faults)
hypotheses.signature: Horizontal-gradient magnitude and a Hessian step/ridge transform on
depth_to_base_surf, corroborated against the cond_surf gradient. A fault that
offsets the conductive basement surface produces a linear step in that surface
even when it has no geomorphic expression at all.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: These are blind or buried faults under basin fill. They are invisible to
the surface geologic mapping that produced the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue
and invisible to lidar, so they are missing from it by construction
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: Both bands are already in the official 19-band stack and both are used
raw by prior sessions, where they rank near the bottom of the
single-channel screen (AUC 0.5302 and 0.5061). No prior raster in the
57-repo registry builds an edge/step transform on them.
hypotheses.cost: low (one gradient + one Hessian transform, reuses cached stack)
hypotheses.status: NOT IMPLEMENTED - budget exhausted; first queued task

hypotheses.title: Multi-scale phase-congruency lineament corroboration
hypotheses.signature: Phase congruency (or a monogenic-signal) transform at 300 m / 1 km / 3 km, then
a corroboration score requiring agreement of location AND orientation across at
least three independent layers. Phase congruency is contrast-invariant, so it
recovers the low-contrast steps that gradient magnitude misses, and
corroboration suppresses flight-line artefacts and drainage networks.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: The USGS Quaternary catalogue substantially predates the GeoDAWN
2019-2021 acquisition. Faults that are only visible in GeoDAWN-class
magnetic and radiometric data cannot be in it. This is the mechanism by
which the sponsor's experts most plausibly drew the test faults.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: The repo has single-scale single-layer transforms only (gradmag_*,
ridge_*, lap_tmi) plus a lidar coherence band coh100. No multi-scale,
multi-layer phase-congruency field exists in this repository.
hypotheses.cost: high (a correct implementation is roughly an hour of work plus a stack rebuild)

hypotheses.title: Radiometric alteration-ratio lineaments (K-metasomatism and U mobility along faults)
hypotheses.signature: Ridge/lineament transform on the K/Th and U/Th ratios. Fault-hosted
hydrothermal alteration fixes K (adularia, illite) and mobilises U, so active
conduits carry a gamma-ray ratio signature independent of lithology, because Th
is immobile and acts as the normaliser.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: Alteration halos survive burial by thin alluvium, where the fault scarp
itself is gone. The radiometric signal is also independent of the
geomorphic mapping stream that produced the catalogue.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: GEMSDOE46 used radiometrics only as a concordance weight fused onto a
r12-scarp-rad-concordance 0.0843). Here the ratio field is the primary
lineament source, not a weight on someone else's field.
hypotheses.cost: low (channels already cached; one ridge transform)

hypotheses.title: Thermal-fluid lineament: alignment of hot springs and geothermometry
hypotheses.signature: Anisotropic alignment statistic (structure tensor or a Hough/Radon vote) over
the 4,118 Hot/Warm springs and wells, weighted by silica and chalcedony
geothermometry. Great Basin geothermal ascent is structurally focused, so
thermal features form linear arrays along the controlling fault.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: Spring and well inventories come from water chemistry and drilling
records, an ascertainment stream entirely separate from fault mapping,
so thermal lineaments point at faults the fault mappers never recorded.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: The repository's thermal channels are isotropic Gaussian KDEs
and in the measured single-channel screen both score at chance
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: low-moderate (only 4,118 informative points over 5.17 M pixels)

hypotheses.title: Lidar-coverage-boundary effort discontinuity
hypotheses.signature: An explicit discontinuity in the detection probability b(x) at the lidar
coverage boundary: inside coverage scarps are mappable, outside they are not,
so the mapping gap should step at the boundary.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: Purely an ascertainment effect - the missed faults are the ones outside
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: Prior work uses lidar validity as a mask. Using it as an effort
covariate with an estimated coefficient, as Phillips et al. 2009
prescribe, has not been done here.
hypotheses.status: DEFERRED - sign cannot be determined offline. If the sponsor's experts also used
lidar to draw the test faults, the coefficient is positive, not negative, and the
arm would actively harm the score. This is the one hypothesis whose direction is
not knowable without a scored submission.
